## High Level Overview of Change
This change tightens IOU freeze handling on a few direct `accountSend` paths so they match Payment / XLS-77.
Regular freeze only stops a holder from **sending**. They must still be able to **receive**, and they must still be able to return tokens to the issuer. Deep freeze on either side of a trust line blocks non-issuer sends and receives.
`VaultWithdraw` and `AMMWithdraw` already follow that rule under `fixCleanup3_3_0` (`checkWithdrawFreeze`). Two gaps remained:
1. **Deposits** (`AMMDeposit`, `VaultDeposit`, and the same helper used by `LoanBrokerCoverDeposit`) only checked issuer-side regular freeze. A holder who set deep freeze on their own side could still deposit into an AMM or vault.
2. **`CheckCash`** used `isFrozen` on the destination, so an individually frozen holder could not cash a check. It also treated frozen source funds as empty even when the destination was the issuer, so the issuer could not redeem during a freeze.

comments.author: ckeshava
comments.body:
### AMM full-withdrawal can zero out a live pool's trading fee

**What the code does.** `updateAMMVoteSlotsAndFee` recomputes the pool fee as a holdings-weighted average of the surviving voters, then **deletes `sfTradingFee`** whenever that average comes out to 0 — the `den == 0` → `else` branch in `AMMHelpers.cpp` (~918–921).

**The bug.** `den == 0` does **not** mean the pool is empty. It means *no account that currently holds a vote slot still holds LP tokens*. The voter set and the LP set can be disjoint, because a deposit into an already-live pool grants LP tokens but **no vote slot** (`AMMDeposit.cpp:541` — `initializeFeeAuctionVote` only runs when `lptAMMBalance == 0`). The withdraw call site even gates on `newLPTokenBalance != 0` (`AMMWithdraw.cpp:483`), so the code is guaranteed to be looking at a *funded* pool when it deletes the fee.

**Repro.**
1. Alice creates AMM(XRP/USD) with `TradingFee = 1000` (1%) → she is the sole voter.
2. Bob deposits into the now-live pool → receives LP tokens, but **no** vote slot. `VoteSlots` is still `{Alice}`.
3. Alice withdraws everything. Bob still holds LP tokens, so the pool stays alive and `updateAMMVoteSlotsAndFee` runs. Alice's slot is pruned → zero surviving voters → `den == 0` → `fee = 0` → `sfTradingFee` deleted.

**Impact.** Bob's fully-funded pool now trades at **0% forever** (until someone votes or bids again). This is strictly worse than the stale-vote bug being fixed: instead of Alice's vote lingering at 1%, the fee is wiped to 0 and any trader/arbitrageur swaps against Bob's liquidity for free. It's also reachable on **existing** pools — any pool already carrying a stale vote slot (from the very bug this PR fixes) can have its fee zeroed by *anyone's* 1-drop withdrawal once the amendment activates.

**Root cause.** An average over an empty voter set is undefined, but the code treats it as a genuine 0% vote and removes the fee. When no voters survive, it should **leave `sfTradingFee` unchanged** (keep the last governance-set value, let the next `AMMVote` decide) — never delete it while the pool still holds liquidity.

**Related gaps.**
- The same path writes an **empty `sfVoteSlots` array**, a ledger shape nothing else produces, which makes `amm_info` silently drop `vote_slots` for a live pool (`AMMInfo.cpp:215`).
- `testFeeVoteWithdraw` never exercises `den == 0` (it always keeps two live voters), so the entire branch is untested.

prs.body:
## Summary

Implement a Concentrated Liquidity Automated Market Maker (CLAMM) for the XRP Ledger, as specified in [XLS-99](https://github.com/XRPLF/XRPL-Standards/pull/498). Unlike XLS-30 which distributes liquidity uniformly, CLAMM allows LPs to concentrate capital within specific price ranges for up to 4000x capital efficiency improvement.

### Ledger Entries (4 new)

- **CLAMM** (`0x008A`): Pool state -- current tick, sqrt price, active liquidity, fee tier, auction slot
- **CLAMMTick** (`0x008B`): Per-tick liquidity boundaries and fee growth tracking (sparse storage)
- **CLAMMPosition** (`0x008C`): LP position linked to NFToken (XLS-20) -- tick range, liquidity, uncollected fees
- **CLAMMTickBitmap** (`0x008D`): Compressed 256-bit bitmap for efficient initialized tick lookup

### Transactions (9 new)

| Type | ID | Description |
|------|----|-------------|
| CLAMMCreate | 85 | Create pool with asset pair, fee tier, initial price |
| CLAMMDeposit | 86 | Add liquidity within a price range, mint position NFToken |
| CLAMMWithdraw | 87 | Remove liquidity, burn NFToken on full withdrawal |
| CLAMMSwap | 88 | Direct swap through a pool |
| CLAMMCollectFees | 89 | Collect accumulated fees without removing liquidity |
| CLAMMVote | 90 | Vote on trading fee parameters (liquidity-weighted) |
| CLAMMBid | 91 | Bid for auction slot (discounted fees, MEV protection) |
| CLAMMDelete | 92 | Remove empty pools from ledger (multi-call for large pools) |
| CLAMMClawback | 93 | Issuer clawback of tokens from holder CLAMM positions |

### RPCs (4 new)

- `clamm_info`: Pool information (by pool_id or asset/asset2/fee_tier)
- `clamm_positions`: Query positions by account or nftoken_id
- `clamm_ticks`: Query tick data within a range
- `clamm_quote`: Swap quote simulation

### Key Design Decisions

- **Fee tiers**: 4 predefined tiers (0.01%, 0.05%, 0.30%, 1.00%) linked to tick spacing, preventing scam pools
- **NFToken positions**: Reuses XLS-20 infrastructure for unique, tradeable LP positions
- **Payment engine integration**: CLAMMLiquidity/CLAMMOffer enable automatic routing through CLAMM pools alongside DEX and XLS-30 AMM
- **Continuous auction**: Adapted from XLS-30 for MEV protection
- **Math precision**: Q64.96 fixed-point with boost::multiprecision (uint128/uint256/uint512)

### Amendment

Feature flag: `featureCLAMM`

## Test Plan

- [x] Unit tests: pool lifecycle, deposits, withdrawals, swaps, fees, voting, bidding (`CLAMM_test.cpp` -- 4881 lines)
- [x] Payment routing tests (`CLAMMPayment_test.cpp`)
- [x] Tick bitmap navigation tests (`CLAMMBitmap_test.cpp`)
- [x] Fuzz tests: random deposit/withdraw/swap sequences (`CLAMMFuzz_test.cpp`)
- [x] Invariant tests (ValidCLAMM)
- [x] Cross-feature tests (NFToken transfer, freeze, clawback)

## Related

- Spec: https://github.com/XRPLF/XRPL-Standards/pull/498
- Discussion: https://github.com/XRPLF/XRPL-Standards/discussions/427

prs.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

A credential issued to a Vault, LoanBroker, or AMM pseudo-account can never be accepted or deleted by it, because pseudo-accounts can't sign transactions. The credential stays pinned in the pseudo-account's owner directory and blocks deletion of the owning object, locking up its owner reserve. Creating such a credential is now rejected on its own amendment; this change adds the cleanup for pins that predate that rejection.

### Context of Change

`VaultDelete` and `LoanBrokerDelete` require the pseudo-account's owner directory to be empty and fail with `tecHAS_OBLIGATIONS` when a stale credential is still linked there. AMM fails earlier and harder: a sole-LP withdrawal walks the AMM account's owner directory and returns `tecINTERNAL` on the unexpected credential, so a pinned AMM can't even be fully withdrawn.

Behind a new amendment, `VaultDelete` and `LoanBrokerDelete` delete any credentials pinned to the pseudo-account before removing it. The cleanup is bounded per transaction; a large pin resumes across multiple transactions via `tecINCOMPLETE`. `deleteAMMTrustLines` removes AMM's pinned credentials the same way, and the sole-LP withdrawal check now ignores credential entries so a pinned AMM can still be withdrawn.

### API Impact

- [ ] Public API: New feature (new methods and/or new fields)
- [ ] Public API: Breaking change (in general, breaking changes should only impact the next api_version)
- [x] `libxrpl` change (any change that may affect `libxrpl` or dependents of `libxrpl`)
- [ ] Peer protocol change (must be backward compatible or bump the peer protocol version)

## Test Plan

Added tests to the Vault, LoanBroker, and AMM suites: each pins a credential to the pseudo-account, confirms deletion is blocked, then activates the amendment and confirms the object deletes cleanly with the credential removed. A further test pins more credentials than the per-transaction bound and confirms cleanup finishes across two transactions.

## High Level Overview of Change

Fixes a rounding vulnerability in `AMMClawback` where clawing back a fractional amount of an integer-based Multi-Purpose Token (MPT) could silently result in zero tokens being recovered, while still burning the target's LP tokens.

### Context of Change
The guard is gated behind the `fixCleanup3_4_0` amendment.

MPTs are integer-denominated, so for integer MPT pools the proportional clawback math (`clawAmount / amountBalance`) can produce a fraction that floors `amountRounded` — or `amount2Rounded` — down to `0`. Unlike its sibling routine (`equalWithdrawTokens`), this function lacked a guard to check for a zero result. Consequently, the transaction would return `tesSUCCESS`, burn the target holder's LP tokens, withdraw the paired asset, but leave the zero-rounded side of the pool completely untouched. This silently caused a 100% loss of the issuer's intended recovery and redistributed that value to the remaining passive LPs.

The fix simply mirrors the existing `beast::kZero` check from `equalWithdrawTokens`. If the rounded asset extraction evaluates to zero, the transaction safely aborts and returns `tecAMM_FAILED`.

### API Impact

- [ ] Public API: New feature (new methods and/or new fields)
- [ ] Public API: Breaking change (in general, breaking changes should only impact the next api_version)
- [x] `libxrpl` change (any change that may affect `libxrpl` or dependents of `libxrpl`)
- [ ] Peer protocol change (must be backward compatible or bump the peer protocol version)

## Before / After

**Before:**
With `fixCleanup3_4_0` disabled, an AMMClawback targeting an integer MPT that rounds to zero returns `tesSUCCESS`. The target's LP is burned, paired XRP is paid out, but 0 MPT is extracted, silently enriching the remaining pool LPs.

**After:**
With fixCleanup3_4_0 enabled, the AMM identifies the one-sided withdrawal caused by the rounding error, catches the zero value, and returns tecAMM_FAILED. The transaction aborts cleanly, leaving all balances untouched so the issuer can retry with a larger clawback amount.

## Test Plan
Added the testAMMClawbackAmountRoundsToZero unit test to AMMClawbackMPT_test.cpp, run across three amendment combinations:

1. Both amendments on (fixAMMClawbackRounding + fixCleanup3_4_0): the rounded MPT amount drops to zero, the new guard triggers tecAMM_FAILED, and pool balances, outstanding amounts, and LP tokens are all left unchanged.
2. fixCleanup3_4_0 off (guard disabled): reproduces the silent-zero bug — the clawback returns tesSUCCESS, burns the holder's LP, but recovers 0 MPT.
3. fixAMMClawbackRounding off: the pre-rounding path decrements the MPT pool by the whole integer and claws back normally.

## High Level Overview of Change

The invariant check condition:
``(!isAMMLine || globalFreeze) && hasPrivilege(tx, overrideFreeze)``
evaluates to false when `isAMMLine=true `and `globalFreeze=false`. This means `AMMClawback` cannot override individual or deep freeze on AMM trust lines (between the AMM pseudo-account and the issuer). The `withdraw()` call succeeds because it uses `FreezeHandling::fhIGNORE_FREEZE`, but the invariant checker then rejects the transaction because it detects a balance change on a frozen AMM line without the override condition being met. This creates a contradiction where the issuer's freeze action prevents their own clawback from the AMM pool.

When the issuer individually freezes their AMM trust line (via TrustSet targeting the AMM pseudo-account with `tfSetFreeze`), all subsequent AMMClawback transactions against any holder in that pool will fail at the invariant check. Combined with the fact that a frozen holder cannot withdraw via regular AMMWithdraw, this creates a freeze/clawback deadlock where LP tokens are effectively locked until the issuer unfreezes the AMM line.


### Context of Change
Change from:
```if ((!isAMMLine || globalFreeze) && hasPrivilege(tx, overrideFreeze))```
to:
```if (hasPrivilege(tx, overrideFreeze))```
The overrideFreeze privilege is already restricted to AMMClawback transactions only (via transactions.macro), so removing the AMM line check is safe.

it's the existing  `minSlotPrice`  formula with the trading fee replaced by the smallest representable non-zero fee.

The normal min price (line 207) is:
`minSlotPrice = lptAMMBalance * getFee(tradingFee) / kAuctionSlotMinFeeFraction;`
When  `tradingFee == 0` ,  `getFee(0) == 0` , so  `minSlotPrice == 0 ` — that's the bug (slot acquirable for free). The fix substitutes  `getFee(1)`  (per  `getFee` 's doc,  `1`  = 0.001%, the smallest non-zero fee):

So a zero-fee pool is priced as if it had the minimum non-zero fee. This keeps the floor consistent with the existing pricing (scales with pool size, continuous with the  fee == 1  case) instead of introducing a magic constant.


For simply prohibit when fee == 0, I believe prohibiting the bid would require a new tec error path and a larger behavioral break. I'm not sure if this is expected.

We recently merged a refactor to `develop` that enables clang-tidy's `readability-identifier-naming`. Your branch now has heavy conflicts that are largely mechanical. Below is a workflow that aligns your branch's naming with develop _before_ merging, which should minimize the merge conflicts.

## One-time setup

If you don't already have clang-tidy working in your env, on macOS:

```bash
brew install llvm@21
# Follow brew's hint to put $(brew --prefix llvm@21)/bin on PATH so run-clang-tidy is found.
```

## Workflow on your branch (before merging develop)

**1. Grab the new `.clang-tidy` from develop without pulling anything else.** Sync your fork on GitHub first, then:

```bash
git remote -v   # should show 'upstream' among others; if not:
# git remote set-url upstream git@github.com:XRPLF/rippled.git
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/develop -- .clang-tidy
```

**2. Reconfigure conan/cmake so `compile_commands.json` is fresh.**

**3. Apply renames for the files modified in your PR:**

```bash
git diff --name-only $(git merge-base HEAD upstream/develop) HEAD \
  | grep -E '\.(cpp|h|hpp|ipp)$' \
  | xargs run-clang-tidy -p build -fix -allow-no-checks
# or -p .build, or whatever your build dir is called
```

**4. Build + test, then commit as a single dedicated commit:**

```bash
cmake --build build -j8
git commit -am "refactor: Align identifier naming with develop"
```

**5. Now merge develop:**

```bash
git merge upstream/develop
```

## Extra

Run clang-tidy once more after the merge to catch any stragglers introduced from develop's side:

```bash
run-clang-tidy -p build -fix -allow-no-checks src tests
# or -p .build, or whatever your build dir is called
```
